system.name: CCF
system.one_liner: a confidential, permissioned framework for building highly available stateful services on trusted hardware, using a Raft-based consensus protocol

content.subject: how CCF extends Raft's Follower/Candidate/Leader state machine with a Joiner state and the CheckQuorum/ProposeVote extensions

elements.name: Join
elements.role: external event admitting a new node into the network

elements.name: Joiner
elements.role: CCF-added state for a node bootstrapping into the network before it has caught up

elements.name: Follower
elements.role: Raft's passive replica state that replicates the leader's log

elements.name: Candidate
elements.role: Raft's state for a node campaigning for leadership

elements.name: Leader
elements.role: Raft's state for the node proposing and replicating new transactions

relations.what: a new node is admitted to the network
Receive AE: the joiner catches up via AppendEntries and becomes a follower
election timeout with no leader heartbeat
candidate wins a strict majority of votes
CheckQuorum: leader steps down after not hearing back from a quorum within a time period
ProposeVote: a retiring leader nominates a successor, fast-tracking the election
Restart: candidate restarts its own election
Discover new term: follower updates its current term
Discover new term: candidate steps down on learning of a higher term
Discover new term: leader steps down on learning of a higher term
Force become primary (an administrative override not detailed in the excerpted text)

content.key_idea: CCF extends Raft's Follower/Candidate/Leader state machine with a Joiner bootstrapping state and two protocol extensions, CheckQuorum (a leader steps down without a quorum) and ProposeVote (a retiring leader fast-tracks a successor), drawn as dashed additions over Raft's solid original states and transitions.
content.reading_order: starts at Joiner (top left) via Join/Receive AE, then follows the circled ①-④ transitions around the Follower/Candidate/Leader triangle

palette.used_for: pale purple fill of the Follower, Candidate and Leader boxes (Raft's original states)
medium purple stroke of those boxes and Raft's original solid transition arrows
pale orange fill of the Joiner box (CCF's added state)
dark gold stroke of the Joiner box border and CCF's additional dashed transition arrows/labels

style.stroke: ~1.5-2pt; solid purple for Raft's original boxes/arrows, dashed gold for CCF's additions
style.arrows: open arrowheads on curved routes among the four states; solid purple for Raft-original transitions, dashed gold for CCF additions; four transitions carry small circled numbers ①-④

encoding.color_means: purple = Raft's original states/transitions (Follower, Candidate, Leader and their core edges); gold/orange = CCF's additions (the Joiner state and its edges, plus the CheckQuorum and ProposeVote extensions)
encoding.line_style_means: per the caption, solid lines/boxes are Raft's original states and transitions; dashed lines/boxes are CCF's additional states and transitions
encoding.state_means: Raft's three original roles are purple solid boxes; CCF's added Joiner role is a pale-orange dashed box
encoding.marker_means: circled numbers ①-④ mark the four transitions the paper text calls out explicitly (election timeout, win election, check quorum, propose vote)
encoding.emphasis: dashing isolates exactly what CCF layered on top of vanilla Raft, letting the reader see the extension without losing the familiar Raft skeleton
reusable_patterns: a well-known protocol's state machine redrawn in the same layout, using solid vs dashed styling to isolate a paper's extensions
weaknesses: three same-named 'Discover new term' edges appear at different places in the diagram, and 'Force become primary' is unlabelled in the paper text, so their exact direction and solid/dashed status are harder to confirm than the numbered transitions

evidence: a leader steps down if it does not hear back from a quorum of nodes within a specified time period
CCF also adds a message to the protocol, ProposeVote which is utilized by a retiring leader to nominate a successor
CCF's additional states and transitions are shown with dashed lines

summary: Figure 1 of the CCF verification paper redraws Raft's classic Follower/Candidate/Leader role state machine and overlays CCF's extensions on top of it. Solid purple boxes and arrows are Raft's original states and transitions: a Follower becomes a Candidate on election timeout (①), and a Candidate becomes Leader on winning a majority vote (②). Dashed gold elements are CCF's additions: a new Joiner state that a node passes through while bootstrapping (entered via Join, promoted to Follower on Receive AE), the CheckQuorum extension where a Leader steps down to Follower after failing to hear from a quorum (③), and the ProposeVote extension where a retiring Leader nominates a successor Candidate to fast-track re-election (④). By keeping Raft's familiar triangle layout and only changing line style and colour for the new parts, the figure lets a reader familiar with Raft see exactly what CCF changed.
summary_zh: 该图在Raft的角色状态机上叠加CCF扩展：紫色实线为原有的①选举超时、②赢得选举；金色虚线为CCF新增的Joiner状态、③失去法定人数降级、④指定继任者投票。
notes: Follower/Candidate/Leader and edges ①/② are Raft-original (solid, purple); Joiner, Join, Receive AE, and edges ③ (Check quorum) / ④ (Propose vote) are CCF additions per the caption and text. The direction and solid/dashed status of 'Force become primary' and the three 'Discover new term' edges are inferred from the image layout only, since the excerpted paper text does not name them; treat that part of the record with lower confidence.
